origin: the three-way run failed for a specific reason (measured-target assist is a collapsed initial state, non-foot 80.8 W), and it also moved the bottleneck: at a 1 ms tick with doubled authority the slip is now 1.50 (2x the gate instead of 7x) while non-foot contact is 73.7 W and COM .630. So constrain what is actually failing now, with cold-start training, which the evidence says is the better distribution.

runs.nonfoot: lagrangian on the windowed maximum non-foot contact over 10 ticks, target 4.889 W, dual ascent 0.05 per rollout on the mean violation, lambda_max 50
runs.nonfoot_height: the same, plus a second multiplier on max(0, 1.20 - com_z) with the same rule

kept: 1 ms policy tick, base target at 200 Hz, C = 0.02, cold start, derived pad body R=.02, mu=1.5, releasable adhesion 0.25 body weight, reward v4 including its soft height term, 42-joint PPO, 48 updates, gates unchanged
why_not_assist_again: the previous run measured that replaying measured targets drives the body to support .253 and non-foot 80.8 W, so it cannot be the initial state of a training episode
labelling: derived channel plus replacement ANN, never frozen-body acceptance
accounting: every constraint value and multiplier logged per update; full four-second assist-then-release evaluation with stance fractions
